messages:
Juno Health: hitting intermittent 599s on hosted /v1/embeddings/batch since ~2026-03-17T10:30 PST, roughly 25-40% of requests. sample request ids: r_9a1, r_9a2. customer traffic spike started after scheduled batch job.
Lina (Support): sorry about that — we're looking. can you paste a curl or SDK call you used and a sample request id? any region?
Juno Health: curl below, region=us-west2. token is short-lived (rotated every 5m by our infra).
```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rb-embed-1","inputs":["text1","text2","text3"]}'
```
Lina (Support): thanks. Kevin (SRE) I'm assigning — can you triage ingress logs for those req ids and check upstream latency?
oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident PDR-842 triggered (severity=sev2)
Kevin (SRE): looking. initial grep shows upstream_status=599 for those req ids and upstream_latency ~1.2s. keystore lookups spiked at same time (keystore_latency ~1.1s).
Kevin (SRE): probable hot-path: auth cache miss -> keystore call -> slow HSM/keystore -> upstream times out into 599.
Dave (Runtime Eng): that pattern fits: token rotation every 5m + many fresh connections can cause keystore fanout. SDKs doing aggressive immediate retries could amplify.
Maya (Infra): checking keystore service metrics — small restore window at 10:29-10:36 where P95 jumps to 1.3s due to a background compaction job, we didn't schedule it in low-traffic window.
Lina (Support): ok root cause likely keystore compaction causing auth cache miss latency -> upstream 599s.
Juno Health: we saw client retries as well, yes. some requests retried twice then failed. worried about double billing. any temporary mitigation?
Dave (Runtime Eng): temporary mitigations: 1) set SDK retry backoff to start at 200ms and max 2 retries; 2) reduce concurrency on client batch jobs; 3) route traffic to us-east1 if you can. server-side we can enable short-lived extra auth-cache entries for the tenant for 30m to avoid keystore hits.
Kevin (SRE): rolling a config change to bump auth-cache TTL for affected tenant now (tenants/juno-health) — should be live in ~2m. will monitor.
Lina (Support): action list: Kevin -> auth-cache TTL bump (in flight), Maya -> reschedule keystore compaction and investigate compaction params, Dave -> review downstream retry/backoff guidance for SDKs and draft customer note.
Kevin (SRE): auth-cache TTL bump applied at 10:33:18, propagation done. checking errors: failure rate drop from 32% -> 3% over last 2m.
Maya (Infra): compaction job rescheduled and tuned; we set compaction to lower I/O priority and split into smaller passes.
Lina (Support): recommended customer comms: apologize, explain transient keystore compaction caused auth cache misses and elevated latencies that led to 599s; mitigation applied and engineers tuned the job; suggest they lower client concurrency and enable exponential retry.
Juno Health: thanks — please confirm if we were billed for failed requests that retried.
Lina (Support): I'll follow up with billing. initial note: retries that reached backend and produced tokens/embeddings may be billable. I'll escalate to billing and ask for credit review.
Lina (Support): @Dave can you prepare a short SDK guidance snippet we can paste in comms?
Dave (Runtime Eng): pasted snippet: ```python
# recommended backoff
retries = 2
backoff_base_ms = 200
for attempt in range(retries):
    try:
        client.generate(...)
    except TransientError:
        sleep(backoff_base_ms * (2 ** attempt) / 1000.0)
        continue
    break
```
Lina (Support): customer update drafted and sent at 10:40am: "We identified a transient auth cache latency caused by a keystore compaction job; we've applied a tenant-specific cache bump and tuned the job. You should see error rates return to normal. We're evaluating billing impact and will follow up."
Kevin (SRE): monitoring now — p95 latency back to baseline, no further 599 alerts.
Lina (Support): closing loop: billing reached out, will investigate charge windows and propose one-time credit if retry billing is material.
Juno Health: appreciate the quick ops work and the comms. we'll pause the batch job for the next scheduled run as a precaution. :thumbsup:
Lina (Support): noted — reopening thread if anything recurs. thanks everyone.
